Three problems, compounding:

	•	“Google averages 4–6% conversion, let’s be conservative with 2%” — that’s the load-bearing lie. Google Shopping averages around 1.9% across all verticals; home & garden at $125–225 price points runs 0.5–1.2%. His “extra conservative” number is roughly double reality. Halve it and $24M becomes $12M.
	•	SimilarWeb estimates for mid-size sites are routinely off by 2–5x, in either direction. It’s a modelled number, not a measurement.
	•	He never separates paid from organic. A store with 2,700 indexed product pages has an enormous SEO footprint. If most of that 660k is organic search built over years, the entire “just run PMax” thesis collapses — the moat is domain age and index depth, not the ad account. He says “all their traffic is from Google” and lets you assume it means ads.

And every number quoted is revenue. Not once in 26 minutes does he show an ad spend figure or a profit figure.

Typically, the more you spend the more less hanging fruit is available for the algo. It's best to look at your own numbers and improve. But I've seen brands at low spend have a good ROAS or CPA, and when they scale2-4x more, the ROAS and CPA drops as less low hanging fruit is in the auction. When this happens, you can lower budget and gain that same ROAS and CPA again.
